_comment: CF-A-NOTE-IS-NOT-A-RUNG. Drew ruling, 2026-09-28 11:55Z, on PR #2457 ("NEEDS RULING: rename rules -- Panini 2023-2026 + SuperFractor"): canonical rung name is the SINGULAR "SuperFractor" (cap S, cap F -- ASCII). Casing decided by majority + internal consistency, not by fiat: backend/src/services/catalog/variationVocabulary.ts's own FINISH_SPELLING map already pins superfractor -> "SuperFractor"; the committed checklist corpus (backend/data/checklist-parallel-names.json, canonical parallels[].name field, counting each product once) canonicalizes to "SuperFractor" for 60 (sport,year,setKey) products including every 2024-2026 flagship Topps Chrome/Bowman Chrome cell, versus only 7 products canonicalizing to "Superfractor" (low f); the 09-26 census's own shipped LogoFractor ruling already established the fractor-family capitalize-the-second-element convention this matches; and backend/src/agents/beckett/parallelNameNormalizer.ts already normalizes the plural superfractors typo-key to this same canonical singular for the Beckett ingest path. 16 rules below carry this ruling: 8 scan groups (1 topps-chrome-prefixed group covering the 5 setKeys that share that literal prefix, plus 1 rule per each of the 7 remaining literal setKeys that do not) x 2 raw plural spellings ("SuperFractors" cap F, "Superfractors" low f -- applyRule is an exact-string match, so each distinct raw spelling needs its own rule). Split by literal setKey/prefix because rewrite-parallel-names.cjs loadRules refuses a setKeyPrefix rule whose scope.setKeys entries do not all literally start with that prefix (bowman-chrome*, topps-allen-ginter-chrome, topps-stadium-club-chrome and topps-cosmic-chrome do not start with "topps-chrome") and falls back to a single scope.setKey match when no prefix is given. The SuperFractor render-artifact spellings ("SuperFractor 1", "SuperFractor ()") and the compound-rung family ("Gold SuperFractor" etc.) are explicitly OUT of scope for this ruling -- see backend/data/parallel-name-rules/2026-09-27-panini-2023-2026-and-superfractor.DRAFT.json pending block for those and the rest of PR #2457's own still-unruled Panini findings. This file was split out of that DRAFT file (non-draft, ruled-only) per Drew review comment on PR #2457, 2026-09-28.

rules.ruling: Drew, 2026-09-28 11:55Z (PR #2457 review): canonical rung name is the SINGULAR "SuperFractor" (cap S, cap F -- ASCII). Casing decided by majority + internal consistency, not by fiat: variationVocabulary.ts own FINISH_SPELLING map already pins superfractor -> "SuperFractor" (backend/src/services/catalog/variationVocabulary.ts); the committed checklist corpus (backend/data/checklist-parallel-names.json, canonical parallels[].name field, counting each product once) canonicalizes to "SuperFractor" for 60 (sport,year,setKey) products including every 2024-2026 flagship Topps Chrome/Bowman Chrome cell, versus only 7 products canonicalizing to "Superfractor" (low f); the 09-26 census shipped LogoFractor ruling already established the fractor-family capitalize-the-second-element convention this matches. Plural rows fold onto the singular per this same casing. Where the singular row is already present at the target id, this alias renames the plural rows parallel text onto it (HEAL, same id); where a fold would land on an OCCUPIED but distinct id (a genuine twin, not observed in this rules own point-read sample), the lanes existing MOVE-if-absent / RETIRE-if-zero-sales machinery governs, gated on the dual sold_comps sales check per row -- no blanket retire. This rule is one of 16 split by literal setKey/setKeyPrefix group (rewrite-parallel-names.cjs requires every scope.setKeys entry to share scope.setKeyPrefix when a prefix is given, and falls back to a single scope.setKey match otherwise -- the topps-chrome-family census scope spans setKeys with no single shared string prefix, so the fold is expressed as one topps-chrome-prefixed group rule plus one rule per remaining literal setKey) -- see the sibling rules in this same file for the rest of the family.
sources: Census: SuperFractor-shaped rows across topps-chrome + 11 sibling chrome-family setKeys, 2001-2026 (partial: topps-chrome-logofractor, topps-chrome-update-sapphire, topps-chrome-update-series, topps-chrome-sapphire NOT scanned before the run stopped -- see RESULT.md). Fold-key totals: superfractor (singular, any case) = 36,090 rows across 4 raw spellings (SuperFractor 31,472; Superfractor 3,516; SuperFractor 1 662; SuperFractor () 440); superfractors (plural, any case) = 22,982 rows across 3 raw spellings (SuperFractors 17,662; Superfractors 4,913; SuperFractors () 407). Both forms coexist EVERY year 2019-2023 checked individually (e.g. 2023: singular 1,127 vs plural 1,974) -- not a one-off, a systemic split. The SuperFractor 1 and SuperFractor () render-artifact spellings are a SEPARATE, still-open strip-note question (a run-on 1/1-notation and a ladders-page empty-paren artifact respectively) -- NOT resolved by this ruling, which is scoped to the singular/plural spelling fork only.

Point-read twin-check, topps-chrome 2024 card #20: id ...20:superfractor:no-auto:num-1 EXISTS (parallel=SuperFractor, source=checklistcenter-2026-08-29); id ...20:superfractors:no-auto:num-1 DOES NOT EXIST. Sampled card numbers differ between the singular bucket and the plural bucket -- this is NOT the same card duplicated under two ids; different cards in the same product/year carry different spellings, a genuine catalog-wide spelling INCONSISTENCY rather than a per-card duplicate-pool case -- every sampled fold target this rule reaches is a HEAL (id already correct, only the parallel text field carries the artifact), not a MOVE/RETIRE dispatch.

WebSearch 2026-09-27 corroborates the 09-26 census own finding for 2025 specifically: checklistinsider.com and cardboardconnection.com both surfaced in search results for 2025 Topps Chrome SuperFractor; cardboardconnection own indexed prose contains the typo SuperFractrors, while checklistinsider search snippet uses SuperFractor (singular, cap F) -- consistent with the ruling above.

backend/src/agents/beckett/parallelNameNormalizer.ts already normalizes the plural superfractors typo-key to canonical:Superfractor (0.98 confidence) for the Beckett ingest path -- this rule brings the catalogs own stored rows into agreement with that same existing normalization, rather than introducing a new convention.
